<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user wants confirmation that the pipeline will include previous months' data when run next month.

The pipeline subtracts one month from the run anchor date. A run in October will process September data. Manual triggers use the logical date. Scheduled runs use the data interval end. The schedule interval is empty.

Yes. The pipeline always fetches the previous calendar month. October runs will process September data. January wraps to December of the prior year. The target date is calculated at task runtime in Asia/Dubai rather than baked in at deployment.

Do not select an old logical date when triggering manually. That would fetch the wrong month.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes. The pipeline always targets the **previous calendar month**, computed at run time in Asia/Dubai — it is not frozen to August.

If you trigger it in **October 2026**, it will fetch **September 2026**. Same pattern every month:

| You run in | Data fetched |
|---|---|
| October 2026 | September 2026 |
| November 2026 | October 2026 |
| January 2027 | December 2026 |

That comes from this step in `spark_period_env.py`: take the run date, go to the 1st of that month, then subtract one month.

Two details that matter in practice:

1. **Manual Trigger DAG** uses the trigger’s `logical_date`. Trigger it next month with the default “now” date and you get last month. If you pick an older date in the trigger form, you get *that* date’s previous month instead.
2. Year/month is **not** hardcoded in config. Stale `iclock_year` / `iclock_month` pins are stripped; Spark reads `SAAL_REPORTING_YEAR` and `SAAL_REPORTING_MONTH` from the pod at task runtime.

So a normal next-month run is previous-month data. You do not need to change config for that.
